title: Protocol for isolating mice skeletal muscle myoblasts and myotubes via differential antibody validation
protocol: Euthanize mice following IACUC guidelines.
Collect muscle tissue from the gastrocnemius, quadriceps, soleus, and hamstring muscles in both legs from 4–8-week-old mice (typically 4–6 mice).
Transfer collected tissue to an Eppendorf tube.
Wash isolated tissue 2-3 times with initial PBS wash mixture.
Incubate muscle tissue in chilled DMEM-F12 incubation mixture containing collagenase, pen/strep, and Fungizone at 4°C.
Maintain the muscle solution in a 37°C water bath for 10–15 minutes.
Shake the muscle solution at 220 rpm for an overall time of 1.5 hours.
Wash the tissue 3-4 times with PBS after incubation.
Incubate the tissue in warmed secondary DMEM-F12 incubation mixture at 37°C while shaking for 30 minutes.
Grind the treated tissue with a mortar and pestle in the presence of liquid nitrogen after shaking.
Pass the ground tissue through a 100 μm cell strainer, followed by a 70 μm cell strainer.
Centrifuge the solution at 1000 rpm/27 rcf for 5 minutes to pellet the cells.
Dilute the collected cells in PBS at a ratio of 1:15.
Resuspend the diluted cells using DMEM-F12 growth media supplemented with 40 ng/mL bFGF.
Pre-plate the resuspended cells on uncoated dishes for 1–3 hours to reduce fibroblasts.
Plate the pre-plated cells in a Matrigel-coated dish.
Dilute Matrigel stock concentration to 1:15 in sterile PBS on ice.
Apply diluted Matrigel solution to flask/plate and shake/tilt to coat the bottom.
Incubate coated plates at 22°C for 30 min.
Remove Matrigel solution back into its original tube after incubation.
Plate primary myoblasts at approximately 0.8 × 10^6 cells per well.
Add differentiation media supplemented with 1:10,000 bFGF to initiate cell differentiation.
Incubate cells for 4-7 days to differentiate into myotubes.
Replace differentiation media every 2 days, supplemented with 1:10,000 bFGF.
Split cells using 2-5 ml of accutase for 5-15 min based on cell count.
Optional: Infect myotubes with GFP-expressing adenovirus 3 days post-differentiation following previous procedures.
Fix cells by incubating them in 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 5 min.
Wash three times for 5 min using phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Incubate cells in permeabilization buffer for 10 min.
Keep the solution away from the hydrophobic barrier to avoid loss of hydrophobicity.
Wash the slide well with PBS if the hydrophobic barrier is lost.
Include Mouse on Mouse (MOM) blocking reagent at a 1:40 dilution when staining mouse tissue with antibodies raised in the mouse.
Dilute primary and secondary antibodies in a blocking solution according to the manufacturer’s suggested ratio.
Aspirate the blocking buffer and cover the slide with the primary antibody solution.
Incubate the slides for up to 18 h (overnight) at 4°C.
Wash three times for 5 min with PBS.
Cover cells with secondary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer for 1 h at room temperature in the dark.
Keep slides in the dark for the remainder of the protocol.
After incubation, wash the slides three times for 5 min with PBS.
Incubate the cells with 1 μg/mL DAPI diluted in PBS for 5 min.
Wash once with PBS for 5 min.
Aspirate the PBS from the slides.
Place 1–2 drops of mounting media onto the cells.
Carefully place a coverslip on the slide, avoiding air bubbles.
Let the slides dry in the dark for 1–2 hours before sealing with clear nail polish.
Store the slides at 4°C and image within 2 weeks.
Plate myotubes on 35 mm dishes with a glass bottom for light microscopy imaging.
Stain myotubes using an Olympus IX-81 or equivalent microscope.
Plate Myotubes and myoblasts at a density of 20 × 10^3 per well and differentiate for 3 days.
Treat isolated myotubes and myoblasts with 10 nmol/L insulin for the specified time.
Replace media with XF-DMEM supplemented with 1 g/L D-Glucose, 0.11 g/L sodium pyruvate, and 4 mM L-Glutamine.
Deprive cells of CO2 for 60 minutes.
Perform oligomycin treatment at 1 μg/mL.
Measure basal respiration for time points 1–3.
Add FCCP (carbonyl cyanide 4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenylhydrazone) at 1 μM.
Measure reserve capacity and maximum oxygen consumption for time points 7–9.
Add rotenone at 1 μM and antimycin A at 10 μM.
Measure non-mitochondrial respiration for time points 10–12.
After measurement, add 20 μL of 10 mM Tris with 0.1% Triton X-100 at pH 7.4 to lyse cells.
Replace lysed cell solution with 480 μL of Bradford reagent for protein normalization.
Place Myoblasts and myotubes in six-well poly-D-lysine-coated plates.
Incubate cells at 37°C with 2.5% glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer for 1 hour.
Rinse cells twice with 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer.
Fix cells at 22°C using 1% osmium tetroxide and 1.5% potassium ferrocyanide in 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Wash samples with 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer (pH 7.3) for 5 minutes.
Rinse samples twice with distilled water for 5 minutes each.
Incubate samples with 2.5% uranyl acetate diluted in water at 4°C for up to 18 hours.
Dehydrate samples by replacing ethanol with Eponate 12 mixed in a 1:1 solution of ethanol and Eponate 12 for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Repeat dehydration process three times using 100% Eponate 12, each for 1 hour.
Replace media and cure samples in an oven at 70°C for up to 18 hours.
Crack the plate and submerge it in liquid nitrogen.
Use a jeweler’s saw with 80 nm thickness to cut the block to fit in a Leica UC6 ultramicrotome sample holder.
Place sections on formvar-coated copper grids.
Counterstain grids in 2% uranyl acetate for 2 minutes.
Counterstain grids in Reynold’s lead citrate for 2 minutes.
Acquire samples by TEM on a JEOL JEM-1400 operating at 80 kV.
Perform analysis and quantification via protocols by Lam et al. (2021).
